title: PR #54871 added a user notification-option DELETE endpoint that looks up the NotificationSettingOption by id without restricting it to the URL's user, so any user can delete other users' alert notification settings.

vulnerable_findings.explanation: In the DELETE endpoint, a NotificationSettingOption is fetched by `notification_option_id` (a URL parameter) without verifying that the record belongs to the authenticated `user`. findings.explanation: All database queries use Django ORM with parameterized lookups (objects.get, objects.filter, update_or_create). No raw SQL or string interpolation is used anywhere in the diff.

In the DELETE endpoint, a NotificationSettingOption is fetched by `notification_option_id` (a URL parameter) without verifying that the record belongs to the authenticated `user`. Any authenticated user who knows (or guesses) another user's notification_option_id can delete it. The `user` parameter injected by UserEndpoint (which validates the `user_id` path segment) is never used in the query — the ownership relationship between the option and the requesting user is never checked.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `user_id` filter to the query so the option is only retrieved if it belongs to the authenticated user: `NotificationSettingOption.objects.get(id=notification_option_id, user_id=user.id)`. This ensures an IDOR cannot be exploited across users.
